transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Tomas (Redwood SE), Lina (PM, Polaris), Raj (ML Eng), Priya (SRE)
Record: Fireflies AI auto transcript (medium quality)

Summary (auto): quick console walkthrough of Evaluation -> prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B compare. Demo used a synthetic 'patient triage' prompt set Polaris provided earlier. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted for latency and data residency; SOC2/docs action items.

Topics: 1) Prompt set creation and versioning 2) Regression alert thresholds and signal types 3) A/B comparison flows and CSV outputs 4) Alerting to Slack / PagerDuty / Prometheus 5) Pilot scoping and next steps

Transcript:
00:00 - Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll do a 30 minute-ish walkthrough and then leave time for questions, i'm maya from redwood, ae.
00:12 - Lina: thanks maya, excited — quick context, we're evaluating ways to monitor prompt health across our triage flows, main concerns are regression detection and being able to A/B model changes without noisy alerts.
00:25 - Tomas: hi all, i'm tomas on the se side, i'll jump into the console and show the evals flow and the A/B compare. bear with the demo, some labels might be off in the recording.
00:40 - Raj: hey — i'm the one who will run the integration if we move forward, performance and token-cost numbers are our main gating factors.
00:55 - Priya: and i'm priya, security and networking for production — we'll want to know about vpc, kms, and audit log retention.
01:10 - Maya: perfect. agenda: 1) prompt set + scenario creation 2) regression alert rules 3) live A/B compare demo 4) integration and pilot plan. sound good?
01:22 - Lina: yep — go ahead.
01:35 - Tomas: ok pulling up the console — this is the Eval->Prompt Sets page. we uploaded a sample triage set earlier, it's a small set of 120 prompts with expected labels. notice the versioning widget at the top, you can pin a baseline model and then run comparisons against any candidate.
01:55 - Raj: that versioning looks useful — how are expected answers stored? like do you support multiple acceptable responses?
02:08 - Tomas: yes, you can have a golden answer and multiple acceptable variants; scoring supports fuzzy match, token overlap, and custom classifier thresholds. for the demo i switched the scoring to pairwise similarity so you see numeric deltas. quick disclaimer — the demo environment uses a trimmed dataset so latencies will differ from your prod.
02:30 - Maya: also note the Optimize suggestions on the right; the system may suggest batching or a quantized variant if cost/latency tradeoffs look favorable. sometimes in the transcript thing it's shown as 'redwood optima' haha.
02:48 - Lina: about regression alerts — do they do false positive suppression? we had alerts from a previous system that were noisy.
03:01 - Tomas: good question. we have a couple layers: first, you can define the metric (e.g. accuracy drop, hallucination rate, top-k mismatch) and set thresholds; second, you can add a rolling baseline window and minimum sample count; third, alert deduping and severity buckets — so you can silence non-actionable blips.
03:25 - Raj: can we attach confidence buckets per-prompt, so if only low-confidence prompts fail we don't get paged?
03:38 - Tomas: yep, filters let you restrict to only alerts crossing certain confidence bands or only from high-priority prompt tags. you can tag prompts with metadata (flow, priority, owner).
03:55 - Priya: how do alerts get out? slack, pagerduty? prometheus?
04:07 - Tomas: all of those. we push webhook events, a built-in slack integration with channels + message templating, PD for paging, and you can export metrics to Prometheus via an exporter for long-term SLI tracking. the exporter exposes per-route error rates and regression counters.
04:30 - Lina: show us the A/B compare. that's the crux.
04:40 - Tomas: switching to A/B. here's the Compare tab — choose baseline (pinned model v1.12) and candidate (open-model-quant) then select prompt set. results compute a table of metrics and you can drill into per-prompt diffs.
05:00 - Tomas: (demonstrates) see this prompt id 47 — candidate dropped from 0.86 to 0.61 pairwise score; it flags by severity and suggests a sample for manual review. at the bottom you can export side-by-side CSVs with tokens, logits and pairwise scores.
05:25 - Raj: tokens and logits — will that leak any PHI? we're careful about patient identifiers.
05:36 - Maya: good callout — logs/exports can be redacted or disabled in Private deployments; for Hosted we can auto-mask PII and for Dedicated we recommend processing in VPC. we'll share the redaction checklist in the security packet.
05:55 - Priya: for Private deployments, what's the control plane? is it run in our VPC?
06:05 - Tomas: yes — Redwood Private leaves customer control plane in your VPC and the inference nodes can be on-prem or in your cloud account. key management integrates with your KMS and we ship audit logs to your SIEM. there was a note earlier in the doc where 'KV cache' was transcribed as 'K-V cash' so ignore that.
06:28 - Lina: curious about the alert thresholds — is there a recommended default? we don't have a baseline yet.
06:40 - Tomas: defaults are based on model family and dataset size; for new customers we recommend a 5% absolute drop threshold on accuracy or a 10% relative on pairwise similarity, and a sample count minimum of 30. but importantly we support canary windows: you can route a small perc of traffic and only trigger alerts for sustained regressions.
07:05 - Raj: can we tie alerts to rollbacks or auto-fallbacks? we need to avoid exposing bad model updates.
07:14 - Tomas: yes, we have automated rollback policies in Redwood Console — if the candidate model crosses a severity threshold for N minutes, traffic automatically falls back to the pinned baseline. rollback is configurable per-route.
07:30 - Priya: that's helpful. on networking, we need to know Egress IPs for the hosted case — any doc?
07:42 - Maya: yes we'll include egress IP ranges and the VPC setup guide in the security pack.
07:50 - Lina: can we demo a small A/B with a real sample? we redacted a few triage prompts earlier.
08:02 - Tomas: sure — loading Polaris sample set. computing compare — this may take a minute depending on size.
08:30 - Tomas: okay results— notable things: average pairwise delta was -0.04 but a handful of high-priority prompts had -0.25. I'm toggling the severity filter to only show priority=high.
08:52 - Lina: that list is exactly what we need to triage with product owners.
09:05 - Raj: export please.
09:12 - Tomas: exported CSV and pushed to the shared link (redwood-demo/polaris/ab-exports). note: CSV includes tokenized outputs and similarity scores.
09:30 - Raj: what's the file retention policy on the hosted exports? we can't keep raw outputs for more than 30 days without approvals.
09:40 - Maya: hosted default retention is 90 days, but you can change retention per-account and we can set shorter retention for Sensitive customers; we'll include this in the SOC2/security packet.
09:55 - Lina: question on cost — how do A/B runs or evals affect token billing? we want to budget for a pilot.
10:07 - Tomas: eval compute is billed separately as evaluation units. a small 120 prompt A/B compare is typically low-cost; for production you can use sampling and incremental checks. for the pilot we can give a cost estimate for both Hosted and Dedicated.
10:25 - Priya: if we do Dedicated, will we still get the Console UI and alerting?
10:33 - Tomas: yes, Console and Optimize are the same surface; Dedicated is about reserved inference capacity and isolation. for Dedicated we also expose an options page for autoscale and bursting.
10:48 - Lina: are there any limitations on the kinds of metrics we can compute? we have some custom heuristics and would love to plug them in.
11:00 - Tomas: you can upload custom metric scripts (JS/Python) that run in a sandboxed evaluator or you can push metric results via API if you already compute them offline. we also support webhooks for post-processing.
11:18 - Raj: about automated regressions — do you support hypothesis-based alerts? like only alert if drop persists across multiple related prompts?
11:32 - Tomas: yes, you can group prompts into scenarios and set aggregation rules: e.g. average drop across scenario > threshold AND > X impacted prompts. that reduces false positives on individual flukes.
11:47 - Maya: quick pause — any other security blockers?
11:51 - Priya: data residency for EU patients — we might need EU region hosting and logs to stay in-region.
12:00 - Tomas: we have EU regions and region-scoped deployments; for Private on-prem we can guarantee no egress. we'll include region options in the proposal.
12:12 - Lina: ok next steps?
12:16 - Maya: proposed POC: 2-week pilot, Dedicated 3-node config with baseline pin and A/B compare on your triage set; we'll run an initial ab-run and set up Slack alerts. deliverables: pricing, SOC2 + network checklist, demo export link.
12:35 - Lina: that timeline works if we get security docs quickly.
12:40 - Raj: i'll share prompt-set and some sample traffic; we need the Tomas-run A/B before kickoff so we have baseline numbers.
12:50 - Tomas: i'll schedule the A/B run and share results.
13:00 - Priya: i'll review network checklist and confirm firewall changes.
13:05 - Maya: cool, i'll send pricing and SOC2 by Friday.

Final recap (auto): see action items. customer interested in pilot, wants SOC2 and network doc, requested A/B run and CSV export.

End of transcript.
